faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.h1: Everything you need to know about Nuktah.
faqPage.lead: Short answers, grouped by topic — the questions teachers ask most.

items.a: An app for teachers in Algeria: photograph a handwritten grade sheet, every student matched by matricule, and complete class reports — with PDF export and Excel workbook updates.
Teachers in Algerian schools — it follows the local grading system: three grade parts (continuous, test, exam), with wilaya, school and class structure.

items.q: How do I import an Excel sheet?
items.a: From the import screen: pick the ministry file (.xlsx or .xls) — classes and students are created automatically. Your first import is free; later ones draw from your credits.
Excel files in .xlsx and .xls from the original ministry template — for all three levels (primary, middle school, secondary) — with student columns and matricules.

Open the camera and photograph the sheet — results are read by the OCR service, which needs an internet connection. A scan credit is consumed only after the read succeeds, never on capturing the photo.

items.q: Can I review results before saving?
items.a: Yes — the review screen shows every row matched by matricule before anything is saved, and you can correct any value by hand. Nothing is written without your confirmation.

items.q: Can I edit student or grade information?
items.a: Yes — students from the students screen, and any grade by tapping it on the grades screen; changes apply immediately.

items.q: What should I do if an import fails?
items.a: Check that the file follows the ministry template and has numeric matricules in the ID column, then try again. If it keeps failing, email us the file name and what happened.

items.q: Does the free version show ads?
items.a: Ads appear only when you run out of credits. You can watch a short ad for one extra credit (up to twice a day) — and the Pro tier is completely ad-free.

items.q: What do actions cost? Do credits expire?
items.a: The free tier covers manual entry, two scans and one import. After that, each scan, import or export costs one credit — and credits never expire.

items.q: How do I delete my account?
items.a: From the «Delete account» page on the web — confirmed by email, straight away and without a support ticket.
Email us at support@nuktah.app — we will get back to you as soon as we can.

about.title: About us
about.lead: Nuktah began with a simple question: why do we write every grade twice?
about.p1: Once in ink on paper, once by fingers on a screen. Between the two: hours of late nights, eyes chasing numbers, and a quiet fear that a grade might land in the wrong place.
about.p2: We knew teachers don't need a new program to learn — they need a tool that understands their gradebook as it is: three grade components (continuous, test, exam), the ministry file in its familiar format, and classes of students with registration numbers.
about.builtTitle: So we built Nuktah on that foundation:
builtItems: You photograph the sheet, and it reads your handwriting.
Every grade is matched by registration number — names can look alike, numbers cannot.
You review every line before saving; the final call is always yours.
You export your class report as a PDF with your school's header, while the ministry file stays exactly as it was.
about.missionTitle: We never wanted to replace the teacher
about.missionBody: We wanted to give teachers their time back — an evening with family, a morning with students, not with numbers.
about.closingTitle: Every mark in its place; the rest is on us.
about.closingLead: Get Nuktah and start with your first sheet — free.
